hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $y=x$

Under this transformation, some points on the star map to another point which is no longer on the star. The star is *not symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A star mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The center is at the origin. The star has a point around zero, nine, a point around nine, three, a point around negative nine, three, a point around negative five, negative seven, and a point around five, negative seven. The equation y equals X is graphed on the coordinate plane. All points are estimates. There are dotted lines showing the location of the image after the shape is reflected over y equals X, but the endpoints of the lines are outside of the current pre image.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $y$-axis

The $y$-axis goes through the center of the star and one of the corner points $(0,9)$. 

Under this transformation, each point on the star maps to another point which is also on the star. The star is *symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A star mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The center is at the origin. The star has a point around zero, nine, a point around nine, three, a point around negative nine, three, a point around negative five, negative seven, and a point around five, negative seven. All points are estimates. There are dotted lines showing the location of the image after the shape is reflected over the y-axis. The endpoints of the lines a part of the current pre image.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the star are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=x$ | No
Reflective symmetry over the $y$-axis | Yes
